abstract: [Proteomics] The rapid accumulation of multi-omics data provides increasing opportunities for cancer biomarker discovery, but the heterogeneity and high dimensionality of these datasets remain major challenges for data integration and analysis. This review examines the application of bioinformatics and artificial intelligence for multi-omics integration in cancer biomarker research. Common multi-omics data paradigms and integration strategies are discussed, followed by a review of the bioinformatics, machine learning and deep learning approaches applied across 84 included studies. Cross-study comparison showed limited recurrence among the reported biomarkers, with only 15 biomarkers identified in at least four studies. Further assessment of the 13 recurrent protein-coding biomarkers showed significant protein-protein interaction enrichment and functional convergence in cancer-related processes, particularly PI3K/AKT and ERBB2-related signaling. This review also highlights current challenges, including missing data, heterogeneity across datasets, limited independent validation and the interpretability of artificial intelligence models. Future research may benefit from integrating multi-omics data with clinical information, pathological imaging, electronic health records, single-cell multi-omics and radiomics, together with broader datasets and greater use of independent validation to support the translation of multi-omics biomarker findings into clinical applications.

abstract: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] Interpretive clinical artificial intelligence (AI), in which a clinician interprets an image or signal and an AI system offers a competing or confirming read, is increasingly routine in radiology, pathology, dermatology, and endoscopy. Oversight of these systems assumes that independent human judgment occurred before AI influence entered the decision. The informatics infrastructure, meaning the electronic health record, its audit logs, and the reporting systems built on them, does not verify this. We name the missing assurance layer decision integrity, situate it between cybersecurity verification and clinical quality review, and argue it is a measurement construct distinct from diagnostic accuracy. Drawing on the logic of preregistration, we propose a candidate architecture, a minimal six-event record under sequential disclosure, preserving tamper-evident evidence of pre-AI judgment, post-AI revision, and rationale. The architecture is a candidate for evaluation, not a validated standard; its purpose is to make clinician independence auditable rather than assumed.

abstract: [Insights into imaging] To evaluate whether large language model assistance improves radiologists' agreement with a text-based reference standard in inferring the modified American Heart Association carotid plaque classification from free-text MRI reports, and whether a lightweight model can perform well under criteria-guided prompting. This retrospective study included 433 patients from three institutions. In a report-based reader study, four radiologists classified MRI reports with and without large language model assistance. In standalone evaluation, a rule-based baseline and 10 models were compared under naive and criteria-guided prompting. The reference standard was expert consensus based on the report text. Among 433 patients (mean age, 65.9 years ± 13.4; 248 males), AI assistance improved six-class agreement with the text-based reference standard. At the vessel level, junior radiologists improved from 61.75% to 83.12% (Qwen3-8B) and 87.75% (DeepSeek-R1); senior radiologists from 77.00% to 87.50% and 92.25%, respectively (all Holm-corrected p < 0.001). Patient-level agreement increased from 41.0% to 78.8% (junior) and from 59.8% to 87.8% (senior) with DeepSeek-R1. Agreement increased (quadratic-weighted κ: 0.231 without AI vs 0.775 with DeepSeek-R1). In standalone evaluation, criteria-guided prompting improved Qwen3-8B agreement from 38.91% to 81.52% (95% CI: 78.87-84.06%), remaining 5.89 percentage points below DeepSeek-R1 (87.41%; 95% CI: 85.10-89.61%). In this report-based classification setting, large language model assistance improved radiologists' agreement with the text-based reference standard, with larger gains in junior radiologists. When prompts explicitly encoded AHA criteria, an 8B local candidate model performed well, supporting its potential use as a standardization aid for text-based workflows. Question Report-based modified AHA classification of carotid plaques is experience-dependent and difficult to standardize, as mapping multi-sequence imaging findings to classification conclusions imposes substantial cognitive load. Findings Large language model assistance improved agreement with a text-based reference standard and raised inter-reader consistency (weighted κ 0.231-0.775), narrowing the junior-senior gap. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B-model agreement (38.91-81.52%), supporting standardized text-based workflows without fine-tuning.

abstract: [Clinical and experimental emergency medicine] Applications of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), are rapidly expanding in emergency medicine, but concerns remain regarding their fairness across diverse patient populations. Fairness extends beyond model accuracy and includes equal performance across patient groups, equitable outcomes and allocation of clinical benefits, and procedural fairness throughout the lifecycle of AI implementation. This narrative review aims to provide a practical framework for understanding and evaluating fairness in emergency medicine applications of AI and LLMs. This narrative review organizes fairness risks into three clinically relevant layers. First, datalevel fairness concerns the data used to train, fine-tune, or prompt AI systems. Biased clinical data, including non-random missingness and stigmatizing documentation, can influence model performance. Second, output-level fairness concerns whether the outputs generated by AI systems are equally accurate, safe, and useful across patient groups. In emergency care, subgroup-specific errors in recommendations, predictions, translations, or instructions may arise from aggregation, learning, or evaluation bias, even when overall model performance appears strong. Third, human-interaction fairness concerns whether the benefits of AI are realized equitably in clinical practice and by patients. Even when data and outputs are fair, inequities may arise if clinicians over-rely on or reject useful AI recommendations, or if patients are unable to access, understand, or trust AI-mediated information. Clinicians should consider potential implications for safety, transparency, and fairness alongside overall model accuracy when evaluating AI tools in emergency medicine.
zh_abstract: [Clinical and experimental emergency medicine] 人工智能（AI），尤其是大语言模型（LLM），在急诊医学中的应用正迅速扩展，但人们仍担忧其在不同患者群体中的公平性。公平性不仅限于模型准确性，还包括不同患者群体间的性能平等、临床获益的公平结局与分配，以及 AI 实施全生命周期中的程序公平性。本叙述性综述旨在提供一个实用框架，用于理解和评估 AI 与 LLM 在急诊医学应用中的公平性。本叙述性综述将公平性风险组织为三个临床相关层次。第一，数据层面公平性关注用于训练、微调或提示 AI 系统的数据。有偏倚的临床数据，包括非随机缺失和污名化记录，可能影响模型性能。第二，输出层面公平性关注 AI 系统生成的输出在不同患者群体中是否同样准确、安全和有用。在急诊诊疗中，建议、预测、翻译或指令中特定亚组的错误可能源于聚合、学习或评估偏倚，即使总体模型性能看似很强。第三，人机交互公平性关注 AI 的获益是否在临床实践和患者中公平实现。即使数据和输出是公平的，如果临床医生过度依赖或拒绝有用的 AI 建议，或者患者无法获取、理解或信任 AI 中介的信息，也可能产生不公平。在评估急诊医学中的 AI 工具时，临床医生应将安全性、透明度和公平性的潜在影响与总体模型准确性一并考虑。

abstract: [Australian dental journal] Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming clinical dentistry, with an increasing number of AI-powered diagnostic and treatment planning tools entering the Australian healthcare market. As clinicians adopt AI-based dental software, it is becoming increasingly important to understand the regulatory frameworks that govern them. This narrative review explores the regulatory approval pathways and governance of AI tools used in Australian dental and healthcare settings to inform and educate practitioners. Australia regulates AI-based dental software primarily through the Therapeutic Goods Administration, which classifies eligible products as software as a medical device under a risk-based, technology-agnostic framework established by the Therapeutic Goods Act 1989. AI tools that function as clinical decision-support systems are subject to mandatory conformity assessment and registration on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG) prior to lawful supply. Although the Australian framework aligns with the International Medical Device Regulators Forum principles, the approval process is comparatively less transparent than that required in jurisdictions such as the United States and the European Union, and questions remain regarding the consistency of post-market oversight. This review also highlights emerging regulatory challenges associated with adaptive AI systems. Software could initially receive approval as a low-risk device that evolves to provide specific clinical advice beyond its approval scope. These updates to functionality risk bypassing established oversight pathways that rely on self-reported intended use. Furthermore, currently available AI tools lack comprehensive public-facing transparent evidence for regulatory compliance that is complicated by ambiguous and inconsistent terminology and adaptive AI system classification. Regardless of regulatory approval, clinicians remain professionally accountable for the use of AI tools in clinical decision-making and for ensuring that patient care meets accepted standards of practice.
zh_abstract: [Australian dental journal] 人工智能（AI）正在迅速改变临床牙科，越来越多 AI 驱动的诊断和治疗计划工具进入澳大利亚医疗市场。随着临床医生采用基于 AI 的牙科软件，了解监管它们的框架变得越来越重要。本叙述性综述探讨了澳大利亚牙科和医疗环境中使用的 AI 工具的监管审批路径和治理，以告知和教育从业者。澳大利亚主要通过治疗用品管理局（Therapeutic Goods Administration）监管基于 AI 的牙科软件，该局依据《1989 年治疗用品法》（Therapeutic Goods Act 1989）确立的基于风险、技术中立框架，将符合条件的产品归类为医疗器械软件。作为临床决策支持系统发挥作用的 AI 工具，在合法供应前必须进行强制性符合性评估并在澳大利亚治疗用品注册簿（ARTG）上注册。尽管澳大利亚框架与国际医疗器械监管机构论坛原则一致，但其审批过程与美国和欧盟等司法管辖区的要求相比透明度较低，且上市后监督的一致性仍存疑问。本综述还强调了与自适应 AI 系统相关的新兴监管挑战。软件最初可能作为低风险器械获得批准，随后演变到超出其批准范围提供特定临床建议。这些功能更新有可能绕过依赖自我报告预期用途的既定监督路径。此外，当前可用的 AI 工具缺乏面向公众的、全面的监管合规透明证据，而模糊且不一致的术语以及自适应 AI 系统分类使这一问题更加复杂。无论是否获得监管批准，临床医生仍对在临床决策中使用 AI 工具以及确保患者护理达到公认实践标准负有职业责任。

abstract: [JMIR medical informatics] Regulatory frameworks such as the Belmont Report, the Common Rule, and the Declaration of Helsinki require informed consent to ensure participants understand a study's purpose and can make voluntary decisions about their involvement. Regulations, including the General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation [EU] 2016/679), further emphasize that consent must be freely given and revocable without disadvantage. Although informed consent forms (ICFs) are intended to be clear and accessible, they have become increasingly lengthy and complex. Large language models (LLMs) offer the potential to navigate and interpret this complexity and have shown promise in biomedical information extraction tasks. However, their susceptibility to hallucinations limits their reliability in high-stakes settings. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can mitigate such errors. This study evaluates the integration of GPT-4.1 with RAG for reviewing data reuse language in ICFs and its ability to interpret complex ICF language. First, we processed 438 ICFs from different trials, including multiple countries, languages, and versions of ICFs. Using expertly curated prompts, we extracted information about data reuse using GPT-4.1. By comparing the LLM-generated data reuse outputs with human expert ground truth, we evaluated accuracy and the time required to extract information for each ICF. To further validate the workflow, we evaluated an independent set of 488 ICFs spanning additional trials, languages, and regions. During the validation phase, the workflow was evaluated using a baseline assessment (89 ICFs) followed by 3 iterative optimization rounds assessed on 14, 281, and 104 ICFs, respectively. For this cohort, we assessed the correctness of LLM outputs along with the quality of supporting evidence provided by the model. abstract: [ACS sensors] Transcription factor-based biosensors are essential for the scalable bioproduction of plant natural products. However, a major bottleneck in developing high-performance biosensors is the engineering of responsive promoters due to the vast sequence space and poorly understood sequence-function relationships. Here, we extend our previously published DeepSEED framework into an artificial intelligence-driven pipeline for efficient and extensible biosensor-responsive promoter optimization. This strategy integrates deep learning with domain-specific biological expertise. By fixing core promoter elements, varying the number and position of transcription factor binding sites (TFBSs) to define promoter backbones, and subsequently optimizing the flanking sequences, we enable the de novo design of promoters. We systematically apply this strategy to optimize a panel of biosensors across different transcription factors and regulatory modes, including four metabolite-responsive biosensors and a quorum-sensing-based environmental sensor. The resulting biosensors exhibit diverse dynamic behaviors with markedly improved sensitivity, expanded dynamic range, and increased maximum output. For instance, the optimized naringenin biosensor demonstrates a 32-fold broader dynamic range and a 27-fold higher maximum output compared to its parent. To illustrate its utility in metabolic engineering, we employed a DeepSEED-designed promoter to dynamically regulate a p-coumaric acid biosynthesis pathway, boosting production by 117.0%. Our work extends the previously published DeepSEED framework into a powerful pipeline for biosensor optimization and delivers a portfolio of high-performance regulatory elements, addressing a critical need and facilitating the development of more intelligent and productive metabolic engineering systems.

abstract: [International journal of molecular sciences] Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease imposing a substantial health and economic burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to address CRS complexity in both clinical and research settings. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines, searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase for peer-reviewed articles utilizing machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing, with a focus on molecular-level or immunologic mechanisms in CRS. Thirty-one studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Our results demonstrate that while AI-driven analysis helps stratify patient endotypes, the identified schemes exhibit substantial heterogeneity in cluster numbers and features, raising concerns about their reproducibility. AI applications also included histopathological image interpretation, drug discovery, biologic therapy selection, and prognostic modeling to evaluate revision surgery risks and olfactory dysfunction. However, using the PROBAST+AI framework, we found that 87.1% of the assessed studies carry a high overall risk of bias, mainly due to the reliance on apparent performance or internal validation and limited independent evaluation of model performance, indicating that many reported performance estimates may be optimistic. Future large-scale, multicenter collaborations integrating AI into clinical workflows will be essential to establish reliable and generalizable AI applications for personalized CRS management.

abstract: Generative AI for medical image synthesis is increasingly used to impute missing data and augment biomedical datasets. Yet despite achieving high computational similarity to their real-world counterparts, synthetic images remain uncommon in clinical research practice, in part because of concerns about their biological validity. Here, we evaluate whether synthetic images support reliable downstream statistical analysis and biological inference in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and multiplexed immunofluorescence (mIF) imaging. We find that associations between patient phenotypes and synthesized images can be severely attenuated. This is because synthesis methods typically omit clinically relevant covariates and therefore generate images that, although visually realistic, mask key biological differences. Furthermore, naive analyses treat synthesized images as if they were observed, ignoring the statistical uncertainty introduced by synthesis. Drawing on multiple imputation theory, we introduce Phenotype Aware Multiple Synthesis (PAMS), an analysis framework that requires no model retraining and instead adjusts synthesized output to recover valid biological estimates with appropriately calibrated uncertainty. Applied to MRI and mIF data, PAMS reduced estimation bias and restored nominal confidence interval coverage. Because it is compatible with existing synthesis pipelines, PAMS offers a practical and rigorous route to statistically and biologically valid use of synthesized images in biomedical imaging research.
zh_abstract: 用于医学图像合成的生成式AI越来越多地用于填补缺失数据和扩充生物医学数据集。然而，尽管合成图像与其真实世界对应物实现了高度计算相似性，合成图像在临床研究实践中仍不常见，部分原因是人们对其生物学有效性的担忧。在此，我们评估合成图像是否支持磁共振成像（MRI）和多重免疫荧光（mIF）成像中可靠的下游统计分析和生物学推断。我们发现患者表型与合成图像之间的关联可能被严重减弱。这是因为合成方法通常遗漏临床相关协变量，因此生成的图像虽然视觉上逼真，却掩盖了关键生物学差异。此外，朴素分析将合成图像当作观测图像处理，忽略了合成引入的统计不确定性。借鉴多重插补理论，我们提出表型感知多重合成（Phenotype Aware Multiple Synthesis, PAMS），这是一个无需重新训练模型的分析框架，而是调整合成输出，以适当校准的不确定性恢复有效的生物学估计。应用于MRI和mIF数据时，PAMS降低了估计偏倚并恢复了名义置信区间覆盖率。由于与现有合成流程兼容，PAMS为在生物医学成像研究中以统计和生物学有效的方式使用合成图像提供了一条实用且严谨的路径。

abstract: Clinical records routinely document medical interventions but often omit the reasoning connecting patient-specific evidence to medical action. This limits the decision-relevant supervision available for training models for personalized care. Here we evaluate a data-augmentation approach that makes selected clinical decision relationships explicit in an 8-billion-parameter Qwen3 model, ChronIQ-DRx2. Using the same training cases and model architecture, expert-guided logic reconstruction was applied across four chronic diseases. On the held-out evaluation, the enhanced model had the highest plotted end-to-end task-completion rate among evaluated systems and higher plotted scores across diagnostic, medication and follow-up measures. The serious clinical error rates shown were 16.7% for the baseline and 12.5% for the enhanced model. In the human-AI evaluation, physician accuracy was 87.40% alone and 88.20% with AI assistance, while mean completion time was 0.959 and 0.780 min, respectively; medical-student accuracy was 62.71% and 74.80%, and mean completion time was 0.210 and 0.195 min. These results are descriptive point estimates; inferential comparisons are not reported here. Structured outputs may make recommendations easier to review, but rationale faithfulness, generalizability and effects on clinical safety require further evaluation.

abstract: [Open heart] Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) is a rare multisystem disorder with marked phenotypic heterogeneity. Cardiac involvement, a major prognostic determinant, often develops years after neurological onset and remains clinically silent in early stages, delaying diagnosis and treatment. We developed a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model integrating clinical, electrocardiographic and echocardiographic data to predict cardiomyopathy in patients with ATTRv but without baseline cardiac involvement. Adult patients with genetically confirmed ATTRv amyloidosis evaluated at four Italian tertiary referral centres between 2011 and 2026 were retrospectively included. Only patients without evidence of cardiac involvement at baseline were eligible. A machine learning model was developed using structured clinical variables, while deep learning models were trained on electrocardiographic and echocardiographic data. These models were integrated into a multimodal ensemble framework. Primary endpoint was development of ATTRv cardiomyopathy (ATTRv-CM), defined as scintigraphy-based diagnostic criteria for ATTR-CM in the absence of monoclonal gammopathy and evidence of left ventricular maximal wall thickness exceeding 12 mm. The cohort included 97 patients (63 mutation carriers and 34 with only mild neurological involvement). Over a mean follow-up of 2.5±2.2 years (IQR 1–3), 15 patients developed cardiomyopathy. Unimodal models showed good predictive performance (all training set area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) in the range of 0.86–0.94, all test set AUC within 0.74–0.89). The multimodal ensemble achieved optimal performance, with 100% accuracy and an F1 score of 1.0, in predicting ATTR-CM. Multimodal AI enables early prediction of cardiac involvement in ATTRv, supporting personalised surveillance and optimised clinical management.
zh_abstract: [Open heart] 遗传性转甲状腺素蛋白淀粉样变性（ATTRv）是一种罕见的多系统疾病，具有显著的表型异质性。心脏受累是主要的预后决定因素，常在神经系统发病数年后出现，并在早期保持临床沉默，从而延误诊断和治疗。我们开发了一种多模态人工智能（AI）模型，整合临床、心电图和超声心动图数据，以预测无基线心脏受累的ATTRv患者发生心肌病。回顾性纳入2011年至2026年间在四家意大利三级转诊中心评估的、经基因确诊的ATTRv淀粉样变性成人患者。仅基线无心脏受累证据的患者符合条件。使用结构化临床变量开发了机器学习模型，同时在心电图和超声心动图数据上训练深度学习模型。这些模型被整合到一个多模态集成框架中。主要终点是发生ATTRv心肌病（ATTRv-CM），定义为在无单克隆免疫球蛋白病的情况下符合基于闪烁显像的ATTR-CM诊断标准，并有左心室最大壁厚度超过12 mm的证据。队列包括97例患者（63例突变携带者和34例仅有轻度神经系统受累者）。在平均2.5±2.2年（IQR 1–3）的随访中，15例患者发生心肌病。单模态模型显示出良好的预测性能（所有训练集受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUC）在0.86–0.94范围内，所有测试集AUC在0.74–0.89之间）。多模态集成在预测ATTR-CM方面达到最佳性能，准确率为100%，F1分数为1.0。多模态AI能够早期预测ATTRv中的心脏受累，支持个性化监测和优化的临床管理。

abstract: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] Artificial intelligence (AI) for thyroid nodules should be evaluated against the decisions it changes, not diagnostic accuracy alone. This critical narrative review examines ultrasound, cytology, histology, and molecular models and distinguishes modality-specific prediction from implemented multimodal learning. The original PubMed/MEDLINE search through 10 August 2026 was supplemented on 25 September 2026 by targeted OpenAlex searches and checks of primary publications, reporting standards, and regulatory sources. Selected studies are compared by sample size, reference standard, acquisition setting, testing design, and performance with confidence intervals where available. We explain feature concatenation, intermediate representation learning, cross-attention, and decision-level fusion, and examine whether integration improves on the strongest component. Reported gains are inconsistent, and complete-case multimodal datasets may exclude the low-risk nodules most relevant to avoiding biopsy. High discrimination for histological malignancy or occult nodal disease does not demonstrate reduced overdiagnosis, fewer operations, or improved survival. A thyroid-specific translation roadmap therefore addresses active surveillance, partial verification and spectrum bias, Hashimoto thyroiditis and multinodular disease, cytology preparation shifts, category-specific thresholds, operator dependence, reporting frameworks, and regulatory change control. The priority is a calibrated, externally tested tool using information available at a defined clinical decision, followed by prospective evaluation of patient and workflow outcomes. A unified imaging-pathology-omics system and reliable AI prediction of surveillance progression remain research objectives rather than established clinical capabilities.

abstract: [Therapeutic drug monitoring] Precision dosing integrates patient-specific factors to optimize pharmacotherapy. However, current evidence often relies on limited single-center studies, restricting generalizability. A narrative review of literature on real-world evidence, pharmacogenetics, biomarkers, artificial intelligence (AI), and privacy-preserving data strategies relevant to precision dosing was conducted. Single-center data are insufficient for robust precision-dosing evidence because of small subgroups and local practice biases. Multicenter privacy-preserving systems enable richer, more generalizable datasets that link doses, exposures, genotypes, biomarkers, and outcomes. However, multicenter collaborations should remain aligned with the intended population and should not imply indiscriminate pooling of heterogeneous data. Secure pooled environments, federated learning, and synthetic data play distinct method-dependent roles. AI supports exposure estimation, phenotype extraction, and modeling of complex relationships but requires rigorous validation against conventional methods. Causal inference requires epidemiological rigor beyond predictive performance. Advancing precision dosing requires multicenter, purpose-specific, privacy-preserving, methodologically rigorous, and clinically validated data systems guided by clinical pharmacologists, with AI serving as a complementary tool rather than a default solution.

abstract: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] The accuracy reported for detecting apical periodontitis using artificial intelligence (AI) is generally interpreted as accuracy against the disease; however, this is usually not the case. Compared with histopathology, single-view periapical radiography detects 16 to 27% of confirmed lesions and 38% with parallax, with a pooled digital sensitivity of 61.0% and a negative predictive value of 41.6%. Two blinded specialists reading 1717 radiographs disagreed on 22% of teeth. Detection depended on lesion size and site: simulated cancellous-bone lesions were invisible below 1 mm in incisors and 3 mm in molars. Of the 44 primary studies identified, 34 (77%) used a label that was a reading of the index image or was unascertainable; eight (18%) used an independent reference-six (14%) suited to contemporaneous detection and two to later treatment outcomes. No cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) input study had a reference independent of its volume. One commercial platform reported 92.3% sensitivity against same-image consensus and 47.9% against blinded CBCT. The reported accuracy is thus in agreement with a noisy rater; recognising this changes what meta-analyses pool. A model that reproduces human labels would have a lower sensitivity against disease than reported; for real-world models, the direction depends on error dependence that the study design cannot identify.
zh_abstract: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] 使用人工智能（AI）检测根尖周炎所报告的准确性通常被解读为针对该疾病的准确性；然而，实际情况通常并非如此。与组织病理学相比，单视角根尖周X线摄影可检出16%至27%的确诊病变，使用视差时可检出38%，汇总数字灵敏度为61.0%，阴性预测值为41.6%。两名盲法专家阅读1717张X线片时，对22%的牙齿存在分歧。检出取决于病变大小和部位：模拟松质骨病变在切牙中小于1 mm、在磨牙中小于3 mm时不可见。在识别出的44项原始研究中，34项（77%）使用的标签是指标图像的读片结果或无法确定；8项（18%）使用了独立参考——6项（14%）适用于同期检测，2项适用于后续治疗结局。没有任何以锥形束计算机断层扫描（CBCT）作为输入的研究拥有独立于其容积的参考标准。一个商业平台报告，针对同一图像共识的灵敏度为92.3%，针对盲法CBCT的灵敏度为47.9%。因此，所报告的准确性与一个含有噪声的评分者一致；认识到这一点会改变荟萃分析所合并的内容。一个复现人类标签的模型，其针对疾病的灵敏度将低于所报告值；对于真实世界模型，其方向取决于研究设计无法识别的误差依赖性。

abstract: [Archives of sexual behavior] There is currently wide variability across U.S. states regarding the legality of abortion with some states having relatively open access to abortion services and others with a total or near total ban on abortion access. Further complicating these state-by-state differences is the variability in policies and procedures with regard to exemptions (e.g., rape, incest) that may allow women access to abortion services that otherwise would be banned in that state. Factors such as a victim's alcohol use at the time of rape and victim's rape acknowledgment may delay or prevent women from seeking medical care post-assault. To help navigate potential confusion regarding state-level policies and requirements to access abortion services following a rape in which they became pregnant, women may use Artificial Intelligence tools, including ChatGPT, for reproductive health care information. Thus, we sought to qualitatively examine information provided by ChatGPT-4o to women seeking information on how to access abortions in each state depending on their alcohol use and rape acknowledgment after finding out they are pregnant following a rape. Using data collected between October 31 and November 11, 2024, we systematically analyzed ChatGPT-4o's responses to abortion access requests across all 50 U.S. states using four prompts that varied by alcohol use and rape acknowledgment, and qualitatively coded responses for accuracy, helpfulness, and inclusion of empathic statements. Results revealed no significant differences in ChatGPT-4o responses across prompt conditions and one difference based on U.S. state level abortion access restriction. Responses in states with more severe restrictions were more likely to include information on rape exemptions than states with less restrictions in abortion access. However, responses often failed to include helpful information and statements reflective of empathic tone, which may exacerbate pre-existing disparities across U.S. states.
zh_abstract: [Archives of sexual behavior] 目前美国各州在堕胎合法性方面存在很大差异，一些州对堕胎服务相对开放，而另一些州则完全或近乎完全禁止堕胎。使这些各州差异进一步复杂化的是，在豁免情形（如强奸、乱伦）方面的政策和程序存在差异，这些豁免可能使女性能够获得在该州原本会被禁止的堕胎服务。受害者在强奸时的酒精使用以及受害者对强奸的承认等因素，可能延迟或阻止女性在遭受性侵后寻求医疗照护。为帮助应对在因强奸而怀孕后获得堕胎服务的州级政策和要求方面可能存在的困惑，女性可能使用人工智能工具，包括ChatGPT，来获取生殖健康照护信息。因此，我们试图定性考察ChatGPT-4o向女性提供的信息，这些女性在因强奸而怀孕后，根据其酒精使用和强奸承认情况，寻求如何在各州获得堕胎的信息。使用2024年10月31日至11月11日期间收集的数据，我们使用四种根据酒精使用和强奸承认情况而变化的提示，系统分析了ChatGPT-4o对美国所有50个州堕胎获取请求的回应，并对回应进行定性编码，编码内容为准确性、有帮助性以及是否包含共情性陈述。结果显示，ChatGPT-4o的回应在不同提示条件之间没有显著差异，但基于美国州级堕胎获取限制存在一处差异。与堕胎获取限制较少的州相比，限制更严格的州的回应更可能包含关于强奸豁免的信息。然而，回应常常未能包含有帮助的信息和体现共情语气的陈述，这可能加剧美国各州之间先前存在的差异。

abstract: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in gastroenterology for endoscopic detection and characterisation, disease-activity assessment, risk prediction, treatment-response estimation and workflow support. However, high retrospective accuracy does not necessarily translate into reliable or beneficial clinical decision support. This structured narrative review examines the clinical development of artificial intelligence across gastrointestinal endoscopy, inflammatory bowel disease, hepatology and pancreaticobiliary diseases through three translational dimensions: explainability, generalisability and clinical actionability. Communication, human oversight and lifecycle governance are considered cross-cutting determinants of implementation. The evidence is most mature in gastrointestinal endoscopy, particularly for computer-aided polyp detection, although benefits vary across operators, indications and practice settings. Applications in inflammatory bowel disease, hepatology and pancreaticobiliary care remain predominantly retrospective, with limited prospective evidence that model outputs alter management or improve patient outcomes. Explainability is commonly represented by heatmaps or feature-attribution methods, but rarely evaluated in terms of clinician understanding, calibrated trust or patient communication. External validation is becoming more frequent, yet geographic and technological transportability, calibration and performance under dataset shift remain insufficiently assessed. Prospective implementation and health-economic studies are uncommon, and available economic evidence is largely model-based. Clinical artificial intelligence should therefore be evaluated as a sociotechnical intervention comprising the model, interface, users, workflow, communication process and associated care pathway. Translation requires clinically defined use cases, representative multicentre validation, human-centred evaluation, prospective assessment of benefits and harms, and continuous post-deployment surveillance. Clinical AI in gastroenterology should complement clinical expertise through transparent, contestable and continuously monitored decision support that preserves clinician accountability and supports informed, patient-centred decisions.
zh_abstract: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] 人工智能（AI）在消化内科中越来越多地用于内镜检测与表征、疾病活动度评估、风险预测、治疗反应估计和工作流程支持。然而，高回顾性准确率并不一定转化为可靠或有益的临床决策支持。这篇结构化叙述性综述通过三个转化维度——可解释性、泛化性和临床可行动性——审视人工智能在胃肠内镜、炎症性肠病、肝病和胰胆疾病中的临床发展。沟通、人工监督和生命周期治理被视为实施的横跨各领域的决定因素。证据在胃肠内镜中最为成熟，尤其是计算机辅助息肉检测，尽管其获益因操作者、适应证和实践环境而异。在炎症性肠病、肝病和胰胆疾病照护中的应用仍以回顾性为主，有限的前瞻性证据表明模型输出可改变管理或改善患者结局。可解释性通常由热图或特征归因方法表示，但很少从临床医生理解、校准信任或患者沟通的角度进行评估。外部验证正变得更加频繁，但地理和技术可移植性、校准以及在数据集偏移下的性能仍评估不足。前瞻性实施和卫生经济学研究不常见，可获得的卫生经济学证据大多基于模型。因此，临床人工智能应作为一种社会技术干预来评估，包括模型、界面、用户、工作流程、沟通过程及相关照护路径。转化需要临床定义的使用场景、具有代表性的多中心验证、以人为本的评估、对获益与危害的前瞻性评估以及部署后持续监测。消化内科的临床AI应通过透明、可质疑且持续监测的决策支持来补充临床专业知识，该支持维护临床医生的问责制并支持知情的、以患者为中心的决策。

abstract: [Oral and maxillofacial surgery clinics of North America] Blepharoplasty and related periorbital procedures sit at the interface of functional reconstruction, esthetic surgery, ophthalmology, facial plastic surgery, and oral and maxillofacial surgery. Because eyelid and periorbital changes can be captured in photographs, videos, and 3-dimensional imaging, artificial intelligence has growing relevance for objective measurement, screening, planning, outcome assessment, and patient education. This review summarizes practical applications and proposes a cautious implementation pathway.

abstract: [Oral and maxillofacial surgery clinics of North America] Artificial intelligence (AI)-based facial analysis enables objective and quantitative evaluation of facial morphology. Recent advances in computer vision allow automated detection of facial landmarks and reproducible measurement of facial symmetry, movement, and emotional expression. Several AI systems, including Emotrics, MediaPipe Face Mesh, Real-Time Facial Asymmetry Analysis, FaceReader, and Affdex, have been applied to outcome assessment after facial reanimation procedures and facial nerve reconstruction. abstract: Cell fate decisions are shaped by dynamic coordination across transcriptomic, chromatin, and protein layers. Time-series single-cell multi-omics assays now enable these molecular layers to be profiled across developmental stages, yet each cell is still observed only once, and the continuous multi-omics trajectories connecting discrete snapshots remain unresolved. A central challenge is therefore to jointly integrate paired omics measurements while reconstructing their shared developmental progression. Here we present Multi-Omics Fate Inference (MOFI), a dynamically constrained multi-omics integration framework designed to reconstruct continuous cell fate transitions from paired multi-omics snapshots sampled across multiple time points. MOFI jointly models omics-specific state dynamics, cross-omics correspondence, and shared population growth within a unified framework, enabling cross-omics perturbation response analysis and identification of candidate cross-omics transformation programs. Across simulated benchmarks and paired RNA-ATAC/RNA-protein time-series datasets, MOFI reconstructed continuous fate transitions, population dynamics and cross-omics changes consistent with observed measurements. In kidney organoids, MOFI captured coordinated RNA-ATAC progression of nephron lineage specification. In hematopoietic progenitors, MOFI predicted perturbation-responsive lineage redistribution and nominated multi-omics transformation programs linking transcriptional modules with protein-level responses. In neural developmental systems, MOFI resolved gradual brain organoid maturation and interneuron lineage allocation during human cortical development. Together, MOFI provides a dynamics-grounded method for converting discrete paired multi-omics snapshots into interpretable models of cell fate progression, perturbation response, and cross-omics transformation analysis.
zh_abstract: 细胞命运决定是由转录组、染色质和蛋白质层面之间的动态协调所塑造的。时间序列单细胞多组学检测如今使得能够在发育阶段中对这些分子层面进行 profiling，但每个细胞仍仅被观测一次，而连接离散快照的连续多组学轨迹仍未得到解析。因此，一个核心挑战是在整合配对组学测量的同时重建其共同发育进程。在此，我们提出 Multi-Omics Fate Inference（MOFI），一种动态约束的多组学整合框架，旨在从多个时间点采样的配对多组学快照中重建连续的细胞命运转变。MOFI 在统一框架内联合建模组学特异性状态动态、跨组学对应关系以及共享群体增长，从而实现跨组学扰动响应分析并识别候选跨组学转化程序。在模拟基准和配对的 RNA-ATAC/RNA-蛋白质时间序列数据集中，MOFI 重建了与观测测量一致的连续命运转变、群体动态和跨组学变化。在肾脏类器官中，MOFI 捕捉了肾单位谱系特化的协调性 RNA-ATAC 进展。在造血祖细胞中，MOFI 预测了扰动响应性谱系重分布，并提名了将转录模块与蛋白质水平响应联系起来的多种组学转化程序。在神经发育系统中，MOFI 解析了脑类器官的逐渐成熟以及人类皮层发育过程中的中间神经元谱系分配。总之，MOFI 提供了一种以动态为基础的方法，将离散的配对多组学快照转化为细胞命运进展、扰动响应和跨组学转化分析的可解释模型。

title: BanglaDiaHallu: Hallucinations of large language models and the effect of guideline-grounded retrieval-augmented generation in Bangla diabetes question answering

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly consulted for health advice, but they can produce fluent statements that are false or unsupported, known as hallucinations, and this risk is poorly characterised in low-resource languages such as Bangla. We measured hallucinations of locally deployable open-weight LLMs in Bangla diabetes question answering and tested whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounded in Bangladeshs National Guideline on Diabetes Mellitus reduces them. Forty patient questions spanning six clinical sub-domains were each answered twice, under zero-shot prompting, by Qwen3.5-9B, TigerLLM-9B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B, and by BanglaDiaRAG, which adds hybrid dense (BGE-M3) and sparse (BM25) retrieval from a physician-reviewed Bangla guideline knowledge base to Qwen3.5-9B. Two physicians rated the 400 de-identified responses by consensus for medical accuracy, completeness, safety, readability and reliability on a 0-1 scale, and responses with accuracy below 0.70 were classified as hallucinated. Hallucination rates were 2.5% for Gemma-4-26B-A4B, 3.8% for TigerLLM-9B, 22.5% for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and 77.5% for Qwen3.5-9B. Guideline grounding lowered the rate of Qwen3.5-9B to 11.3% (difference -66.3 percentage points; 95% CI -76.3 to -55.0) and raised every criterion by 0.24 to 0.38 points (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). BanglaDiaRAG outscored Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on all five criteria and matched or exceeded TigerLLM-9B, but it remained below Gemma-4-26B-A4B in safety, readability and reliability, and its residual errors were specific, confident and potentially harmful. Guideline grounding can turn a weak general-purpose model into a much safer Bangla diabetes assistant, but the choice of base model mattered as much as retrieval and no configuration was free of hallucination, so clinical oversight remains essential before patient-facing use.

title: Balanced Risk Integrity Index: a stratum-level metric for evaluating clinical prediction alerts under competing risks and censoring

abstract: Background: Conventional discrimination metrics, such as the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), do not characterize the composition of outcomes among patients flagged as high risk by clinical prediction models. This limitation is particularly relevant in critical care, where competing deaths and incomplete follow-up can complicate the interpretation of prediction alerts. We developed the Balanced Risk Integrity Index (BRII), a stratum-level metric defined as the proportion of target events among target events, competing deaths, and early-censored observations in a flagged high-risk stratum. BRII is algebraically related to positive predictive value (PPV) and is reported alongside its component decomposition to characterize the outcome composition of flagged patients. Methods: We evaluated BRII using seven acute kidney injury (AKI) prediction models developed in MIMIC-IV and externally validated in MIMIC-III and eICU-CRD (116,010 patients in total). Additional simulations examined the effects of competing deaths and early censoring on BRII and conventional model performance metrics. Results: For 48-hour AKI prediction in the top 10% risk stratum, BRII ranged from 0.90 to 0.96 in MIMIC-III, compared with less than 0.26 across all models in eICU-CRD, where 61.5% of evaluated patients were censored before the prediction horizon. In the eICU-CRD top 10% strata for the same target, 37.0% to 50.2% of patients were censored early, 12.2% to 15.5% had AKI, and 3.4% to 8.1% died before AKI. BRII and PPV ordered at least one model pair differently in 34 of 48 cohort-outcome-top-k groups. Under simulated random censoring for 48-hour AKI prediction, BRII declined by up to 0.80 while binary-label AUROC changed by less than 0.02. Conclusions: BRII provided complementary information on high-risk stratum composition, yielding different model rankings from PPV and revealing substantial differences across external validation cohorts. Interpreted alongside PPV and its component decomposition, BRII offers a standardized approach to evaluating clinical prediction alerts across models and observation environments.

abstract: [Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland)] Objective: This study aimed to systematically review worldwide research on artificial intelligence (AI) applications in emergency medical service (EMS) call-taking and dispatch operations and identify current research trends and research needs. Methods: This scoping review was reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, KoreaMed, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library were searched for studies published from January 2021 to August 2026. Data were synthesized descriptively. Results: Eighteen studies from 13 countries and one multinational setting were included; eight (44.4%) were conducted in Europe. Patient Recognition and Classification was the predominant domain (11/18, 61.1%), followed by Dispatch Support and Operational Decision-Making (5/18, 27.8%) and Other Methodological Applications (2/18, 11.1%). Structured clinical or dispatch data were used in 11 studies, textual data in eight, and call audio in five; four applied multimodal integration. Deep learning (DL) was used as a primary model in 11 studies and classical machine learning (ML) in eight, including three using both; large language models (LLMs) were used in two. Eleven studies involved retrospective model development and internal validation, whereas only two were randomized controlled trials. None of the 11 model-development studies conducted independent external validation or calibration assessment, and the two randomized trials, one with high risk of bias and the other with some concerns, showed no consistent improvement across dispatch outcomes. Conclusions: AI applications span diverse clinical and operational tasks, with multimodal integration, speech technologies, and LLMs broadening their potential scope. Evidence remains dominated by retrospective model development and internal validation; prospective and real-world implementation studies are needed to establish safety and clinical utility before integration into EMS systems.

abstract: [Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland)] Spirometry underuse and persistent limitations in its technical quality and interpretation in primary healthcare (PHC) contribute to delayed and inaccurate diagnosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma. Artificial intelligence (AI) has recently demonstrated, at the randomised controlled trial level, that it can improve spirometry interpretation by primary care clinicians. Maximal mid-expiratory flow (MMEF), a spirometric measure routinely derived from every forced expiratory manoeuvre, has been associated with subsequent airflow obstruction and lung function decline, particularly when conventional spirometric indices remain preserved, suggesting that it may contribute to earlier recognition of small airway dysfunction. However, no existing review has examined whether AI could specifically address the challenge of MMEF interpretation, and the incremental value of MMEF within AI-assisted spirometry models remains unestablished. This narrative review synthesises current evidence on AI-assisted spirometry in PHC across three evidence domains, diagnostic classification, quality control, and computational small airway assessment, and examines the potential for integrating MMEF with conventional spirometric indices, flow-volume curve morphology, technical quality, clinical characteristics, and longitudinal data to support its clinical interpretation. The available evidence supports the feasibility of the individual components underpinning this proposed framework, including AI-assisted spirometry interpretation, automated quality assessment, and computational extraction of small airway information from spirometric data. However, the contextual integration of MMEF within AI-assisted models has not yet been prospectively evaluated, and validation of its incremental predictive value and clinical utility is needed before implementation can be recommended.
zh_abstract: [Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland)] 肺量计使用不足及其在初级医疗保健（PHC）中的技术质量和解读方面持续存在的局限，导致慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）和哮喘诊断延迟且不准确。人工智能（AI）最近在随机对照试验层面已证明，它可以改善初级保健临床医生对肺量计的解读。最大呼气中期流量（MMEF）是一种通常从每次用力呼气动作中得出的肺量计指标，与随后的气流阻塞和肺功能下降相关，尤其是当常规肺量计指标仍保持正常时，提示它可能有助于更早识别小气道功能障碍。然而，现有综述均未考察 AI 能否专门应对 MMEF 解读的挑战，且 MMEF 在 AI 辅助肺量计模型中的增量价值仍未确立。本叙述性综述综合了关于 AI 辅助肺量计在 PHC 中应用的当前证据，涵盖三个证据领域：诊断分类、质量控制以及计算性小气道评估，并考察将 MMEF 与常规肺量计指标、流量-容积曲线形态、技术质量、临床特征和纵向数据相整合以支持其临床解读的潜力。现有证据支持支撑该拟议框架的各个组成部分的可行性，包括 AI 辅助肺量计解读、自动化质量评估以及从肺量计数据中计算提取小气道信息。然而，MMEF 在 AI 辅助模型中的情境化整合尚未经过前瞻性评估，在其推荐实施之前，需要对其增量预测价值和临床效用进行验证。

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center; conditions: History Taking, Artificial Intelligence (AI); type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 250; status: ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION] This study evaluates whether an artificial intelligence (AI) conversational agent called MINERVA (Medical Interface for Navigating the Emergency Room with Voice Assistance) can safely and feasibly gather medical histories from emergency department (ED) patients and produce accurate summaries. abstract: [Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland)] Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) may make surgical information easier to access and understand. However, these tools cannot replace the clinician's role in shared decision-making or the requirements for valid informed consent. Methods: This narrative review follows the surgical patient pathway from diagnosis and explanation to option comparison, shared decision-making, and informed consent. It examines conventional digital tools, LLM-assisted communication, personalized prediction, direct consent studies, patient and professional perspectives and legal, ethical, and governance issues. A formal meta-analysis and study-level risk-of-bias assessment were not performed. Results: AI may support several stages of surgical care. Diagnostic and predictive systems can assist clinicians. LLMs can help explain approved information, prepare patients for consultation, and improve consent materials. Conventional interactive tools have the strongest evidence for better comprehension. Evidence for LLM-assisted consent is still based mainly on simulations and document analyses. Patient-facing use requires source control, privacy protection, and visible clinical oversight. AI cannot establish capacity, voluntariness, or final authorization. We propose a five-level framework in which safeguards increase with clinical influence. Conclusions: AI may support the patient's path from diagnosis to an informed surgical choice when it uses approved information, serves a defined task, and remains under clinical oversight. Current evidence does not support autonomous AI-mediated consent or AI-directed treatment choice. The aim should be a better-informed, preference-sensitive decision, not an automated signature.
zh_abstract: [Healthcare（Basel, Switzerland）] 【背景】人工智能（AI）和大语言模型（LLM）可能使外科信息更易获取和理解。然而，这些工具不能替代临床医生在共享决策中的作用，也不能替代有效知情同意的要求。【方法】本叙述性综述沿外科患者路径展开，从诊断和解释到方案比较、共享决策和知情同意。它考察传统数字工具、LLM辅助沟通、个性化预测、直接同意研究、患者与专业人员视角以及法律、伦理和治理问题。未进行正式荟萃分析和研究层面偏倚风险评估。【结果】AI可能支持外科护理的若干阶段。诊断和预测系统可辅助临床医生。LLM可帮助解释已批准的信息、让患者为咨询做好准备并改进同意材料。传统交互式工具在改善理解方面证据最强。LLM辅助同意的证据仍主要基于模拟和文档分析。面向患者的使用需要来源控制、隐私保护以及可见的临床监督。AI不能确立行为能力、自愿性或最终授权。我们提出一个五级框架，其中保障措施随临床影响力增加而增强。【结论】当AI使用已批准的信息、服务于明确任务并始终处于临床监督之下时，它可能支持患者从诊断走向知情的外科选择。当前证据不支持自主的AI介导同意或AI指导的治疗选择。目标应是更充分知情的、对偏好敏感的决定，而不是自动化签名。

abstract: [The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences] Dental crowding is fundamental to orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning, yet what constitutes "crowding" remains surprisingly heterogeneous. Space analysis quantifies tooth size-arch length discrepancy, irregularity indices characterize alignment displacement, and clinician-assigned severity reflects broader diagnostic interpretation. This narrative review examines the evolution of crowding assessment from conventional space analysis and digital measurement to two-dimensional artificial intelligence (AI), three-dimensional point-cloud learning, and clinician-aware agentic AI. Digitalization improves efficiency and reproducibility but does not resolve fundamental dependencies on how crowding is defined, anatomically represented, and established as a reference standard. Two-dimensional models enable prediction from readily available images but are constrained by projection and scale, whereas three-dimensional approaches directly learn from dental surface representations and can capture local geometric relationships. In a companion study of 495 arches from 284 patients, PointNet++ achieved an R2 of 0.718 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.54 mm for prediction of crowding. In a separate retrospective demonstration, a bounded Gemini-based Agent incorporating matched record-derived verbal information reduced MAE from 1.951 to 1.437 mm, whereas mismatched information degraded performance. These findings also illustrate that the target construct-the specific clinical feature of crowding that a model is trained to predict-may differ across assessment methods. Together, these findings highlight a fundamental challenge: improving prediction does not resolve ambiguity in the target construct. Future crowding AI should therefore align the target construct, reference standard, and input representation; preserve provenance and uncertainty; integrate complementary clinical information transparently; and route uncertain cases for expert review.
zh_abstract: [The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences] 牙列拥挤是正畸诊断和治疗计划的基础，然而“拥挤”的构成却出人意料地异质。间隙分析量化牙量与牙弓长度不调，不齐指数刻画排列位移，而临床医生判定的严重程度则反映了更广泛的诊断解读。本叙述性综述考察了拥挤评估的演变，从传统间隙分析和数字化测量，到二维人工智能（AI）、三维点云学习，以及具有临床医生感知能力的智能体式 AI。数字化提高了效率和可重复性，但并未解决对拥挤如何定义、如何解剖学表征以及如何确立参考标准的根本性依赖。二维模型能够基于易于获取的图像进行预测，但受限于投影和尺度；而三维方法直接从牙齿表面表征中学习，能够捕捉局部几何关系。在一项纳入 284 例患者 495 个牙弓的配套研究中，PointNet++ 预测拥挤度达到 R2 为 0.718、平均绝对误差（MAE）为 1.54 mm。在另一项回顾性演示中，一个整合了匹配病历来源言语信息的受限 Gemini 智能体将 MAE 从 1.951 mm 降至 1.437 mm，而不匹配的信息则使性能下降。这些发现还表明，目标构念——即模型被训练去预测的拥挤的特定临床特征——可能在不同评估方法之间有所不同。总体而言，这些发现凸显了一个根本性挑战：改进预测并不能解决目标构念的模糊性。因此，未来的拥挤 AI 应使目标构念、参考标准和输入表征相互对齐；保留来源信息与不确定性；透明地整合互补临床信息；并将不确定的病例转由专家复核。

abstract: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] Background: Accurate detection and classification of segmental left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) are challenging due to rib and reverberation artifacts in two-dimensional short-axis (2D-SAX) echocardiography view. These artifacts lead to ambiguity in the boundaries of the myocardial region. Existing artificial intelligence techniques focus on global LVH detection compared to segmental LVH classification. Methodology: To solve the abovementioned problem, a curriculum-based left ventricular hypertrophy deep learning (LVH-DL) framework is proposed for segmental LVH classification. The proposed framework was tested with 2000 images of segmental LVH, which consists of (a) apical-423, (b) basal-382, (c) mid-ventricular-349, (d) diffuse-453, and (e) normal-393. The curriculum-based deep learning model consists of proposed algorithms such as (i) preprocessing of Mountaineering-Team-Based Optimization Deep Denoised Convolutional Neural Network (MTBO-DnCNN) for removing artifacts and enhancing the boundaries, (ii) segmentation of modified active contour segmentation (MACS) algorithm accurately extracting the myocardium region from the background, and (iii) classification of curriculum-based ConvNeXt-V2 model classifying segmental LVH using inter-channel features such as valvular structures and chamber size from the segmented myocardial region. Results: The proposed LVH-DL framework achieves a classification accuracy of about (a) 96.5% for apical, (b) 95% for basal, (c) 95.8% for mid-ventricular, (d) 97.2% for diffuse, and (e) 95% for normal. Conclusions: Thus, Thus, the proposed LVH-DL framework acts as a decision support tool for early identification of segmental LVH.
zh_abstract: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] 【背景】由于二维短轴（2D-SAX）超声心动图切面中存在肋骨和混响伪影，对节段性左心室肥厚（LVH）进行准确检测和分类具有挑战性。这些伪影导致心肌区域边界模糊。现有的人工智能技术侧重于整体 LVH 检测，而非节段性 LVH 分类。【方法】为解决上述问题，提出了一种基于课程学习的左心室肥厚深度学习（LVH-DL）框架，用于节段性 LVH 分类。所提出的框架使用 2000 张节段性 LVH 图像进行测试，包括 (a) 心尖部-423、(b) 基底部-382、(c) 中心室部-349、(d) 弥漫性-453 和 (e) 正常-393。基于课程学习的深度学习模型由以下所提出的算法组成：(i) 登山队优化深度去噪卷积神经网络（MTBO-DnCNN）预处理，用于去除伪影并增强边界；(ii) 改进活动轮廓分割（MACS）算法分割，从背景中准确提取心肌区域；(iii) 基于课程学习的 ConvNeXt-V2 模型分类，利用来自分割心肌区域的瓣膜结构和心腔大小等通道间特征对节段性 LVH 进行分类。【结果】所提出的 LVH-DL 框架获得的分类准确率约为 (a) 心尖部 96.5%、(b) 基底部 95%、(c) 中心室部 95.8%、(d) 弥漫性 97.2%、(e) 正常 95%。【结论】因此，因此，所提出的 LVH-DL 框架可作为早期识别节段性 LVH 的决策支持工具。

abstract: [Sensors (Basel, Switzerland)] Vascular access performance determines the adequacy, safety, and cost of hemodialysis. Stenosis, thrombosis, cannulation difficulty, infection, and access-related cardiac stress remain major sources of morbidity. This narrative review examines artificial intelligence and sensing technologies for vascular access care, based on PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov searches through 22 August 2026 with citation chaining. Existing reviews have examined artificial intelligence in dialysis broadly or prediction models in isolation. In this review, the vascular access itself is kept as the unit of analysis, and the evidence is followed across four connected stages: systemic risk stratification; prediction of maturation, dysfunction, and complications from clinical, ultrasound, and multimodal data; longitudinal monitoring with optical, acoustic, vibration, thermal, and pressure sensors; and procedural support with robotics and visualization technologies. Reported discrimination is high in retrospective, recording-level analyses, reaching areas under the curve of 0.99 and sample-level accuracy of 100%, but falls to approximately 0.71 in longitudinal designs that predict future events in the same patients; patient-level external validation and calibration are also rarely reported. No approach has yet been demonstrated to reduce thrombosis, prolong patency, avoid interventions, or lower cost relative to standard care in prospective multicenter studies. Deployment is further constrained by power budgets, duty cycling, and transmission bandwidth in wearable devices. Technical feasibility should not be read as clinical utility.
zh_abstract: [Sensors (Basel, Switzerland)] 血管通路性能决定血液透析的充分性、安全性和成本。狭窄、血栓形成、插管困难、感染以及通路相关心脏负荷仍是主要致病原因。本叙述性综述基于截至2026年8月22日的PubMed和ClinicalTrials.gov检索，并结合引文追溯，考察用于血管通路护理的人工智能和传感技术。现有综述已广泛考察透析中的人工智能或孤立地考察预测模型。在本综述中，血管通路本身被作为分析单元，并沿四个相互关联的阶段追踪证据：系统性风险分层；基于临床、超声和多模态数据预测成熟、功能障碍和并发症；使用光学、声学、振动、热和压力传感器进行纵向监测；以及使用机器人和可视化技术进行手术支持。在回顾性、记录层面的分析中，报告的区分度很高，曲线下面积达到0.99，样本层面准确率达到100%，但在预测同一患者未来事件的纵向设计中降至约0.71；患者层面的外部验证和校准也鲜有报告。尚无任何方法在前瞻性多中心研究中被证明相对于标准护理能够减少血栓形成、延长通畅期、避免干预或降低成本。可穿戴设备中的部署还进一步受到功率预算、占空比和传输带宽的限制。技术可行性不应被解读为临床效用。

abstract: [Journal of clinical medicine] Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly used in periodontal assessment, image analysis, outcome prediction, and clinical decision support. However, evidence specifically addressing gingival recession (GR) and related periodontal soft-tissue parameters remains fragmented and predominantly technical. This scoping review aimed to map AI/ML applications for the detection, measurement, prediction, and treatment planning of GR and to identify methodological limitations and translational evidence gaps. Methods: This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the JBI methodology for scoping reviews and reported according to PRISMA-ScR. Eligibility was structured according to the Population-Concept-Context framework and included English-language original studies involving human participants or human-derived clinical data and evaluating AI/ML approaches directly related to GR or to periodontal soft-tissue or anatomical parameters relevant to its assessment or management. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Embase were utilized as the core bibliographic databases, while Google Scholar was used as an additional search source with screening restricted to the first 200 results ranked by relevance. No restrictions on publication year or start date were applied. Study characteristics, AI methods, clinical applications, validation strategies, and performance metrics were charted and descriptively synthesized. Results: Twelve studies were included across four main clinical domains: detection and segmentation of gingival recession and related soft-tissue features, measurement and anatomical landmark localization, prediction and risk assessment, and treatment planning or clinical decision support. AI/ML models generally demonstrated promising technical performance, including high classification and segmentation accuracy and submillimeter localization of periodontal anatomical landmarks. However, datasets, reference standards, validation strategies, and reported performance metrics were heterogeneous. abstract: [International journal of molecular sciences] Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping molecular oncology by making complex biological data tractable and by extending the reach of precision drug discovery. Its emerging value is particularly evident at the interface of immunoengineering and targeted therapy, where computational models can help prioritize tumor-selective antigens, predict neoantigen immunogenicity, optimize engineered receptors, support antibody and antibody-drug conjugate design, guide small-molecule discovery, refine genome-editing strategies, and anticipate treatment response. Across these applications, the central promise is not automation for its own sake, but a wider therapeutic window in which tumor control is increased while off-target toxicity is reduced. Yet the translational gap remains substantial. Many models are still preclinical, external validation is limited, and clinical implementation remains uncommon. This Commentary follows representative methods across a therapeutic continuum that now extends from target discovery and therapeutic engineering to imaging, liquid biopsy, resistance forecasting, combination selection, and drug repurposing. We argue that clinical value will depend on closed-loop workflows in which multimodal predictions are experimentally validated, externally tested, and longitudinally updated to guide the next therapeutic decision.

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Kastamonu University; conditions: Schizophrenia Caregiver, Caregiver Burden, Emotional Expressivity; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 88; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Schizophrenia is a chronic mental disorder that affects the diagnosed individual and the family members involved in the care process from a biopsychosocial perspective. The course of the illness, the recurrence of symptoms, and the high level of care required can increase the burden on caregivers and make it difficult for them to express their emotions. Structured psychoeducation and cognitive-behavioral interventions have been reported to be beneficial for caregivers in managing these challenges. The aim of this study is to develop an AI-supported psychoeducation program based on a cognitive-behavioral approach for caregivers of individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia and to evaluate the program's impact on caregiving burden and the level of emotional expression. The six-week program will cover topics such as the caregiver role and burden, schizophrenia, the thought-emotion-behavior cycle, recognizing and expressing emotions, effective communication, setting boundaries, seeking support, signs of relapse, and crisis planning. Content based on scientific literature will be evaluated by experts. Artificial intelligence will facilitate interaction with the content, participation in activities, the application of skills, and structured feedback. The system will not provide clinical assessments, diagnoses, or personalized treatment recommendations; participants will be referred to appropriate healthcare services in situations requiring professional evaluation. The study will be conducted using a quasi-experimental design with pre-test and post-test control groups. A total of 88 caregivers will be recruited, with 44 assigned to the experimental group and 44 to the control group. The program will be administered to the experimental group, while the control group will receive routine care. Data will be collected using the Caregiver Descriptive Information Form, the Zarit Caregiver Burden Scale, and the Emotional Expression Scale. A Program Evaluation Form will also be used for the experimental group. The program to be developed is expected to reduce the caregiving burden on caregivers and improve their ability to express emotions. It is anticipated that the findings will contribute to psychiatric nursing practice, the development of AI-supported psychoeducation programs, and the strengthening of psychosocial support provided to caregivers.

abstract: [Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland)] Background: Although artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into nursing practice, little is known about the association between nurses' AI literacy and their subjective workload. This study examines the associations between three dimensions of AI literacy-technical understanding, critical appraisal, and practical application-and overall and dimension-specific subjective workload among clinical nurses. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 305 clinical nurses recruited through convenience sampling from two hospitals in central Taiwan. AI literacy was assessed using the self-report Scale for the Assessment of Non-Experts' AI Literacy (SNAIL), with responses rated on a five-point Likert scale. Subjective workload was assessed using the self-report NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX). Pearson correlation and hierarchical multiple linear regression analyses were performed, adjusting for relevant demographic and work-related characteristics. Results: Higher technical understanding, critical appraisal, and practical application were each associated with lower temporal demand and frustration, and these associations remained statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. More limited associations were observed for physical demand and the overall NASA-TLX workload score, while no robust associations were found for mental demand, effort, or performance. Conclusions: The assessed dimensions of AI literacy are found to be associated with specific dimensions of nurses' subjective workload, rather than with workload uniformly, with the clearest relationships observed for temporal demand and frustration. Further longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine whether improvements in AI literacy are accompanied by meaningful changes in nurses' workload experiences.
zh_abstract: [Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland)] 【背景】尽管人工智能（AI）日益融入护理实践，但关于护士的AI素养与其主观工作负荷之间的关联知之甚少。本研究考察临床护士AI素养的三个维度——技术理解、批判性评价和实际应用——与总体及特定维度主观工作负荷之间的关联。【方法】采用便利抽样从台湾中部两家医院招募305名临床护士进行横断面调查。AI素养使用自评量表《非专家AI素养评估量表》（Scale for the Assessment of Non-Experts' AI Literacy, SNAIL）评估，回答采用五点Likert量表评分。主观工作负荷使用自评NASA任务负荷指数（NASA-TLX）评估。进行Pearson相关和分层多元线性回归分析，并校正相关人口学和工作相关特征。【结果】较高的技术理解、批判性评价和实际应用分别与较低的时间需求和挫败感相关，且这些关联在多重检验校正后仍具有统计学显著性。对体力需求和总体NASA-TLX工作负荷评分的关联较为有限，而未发现脑力需求、努力程度或绩效有稳健关联。【结论】所评估的AI素养维度被发现与护士主观工作负荷的特定维度相关，而非与工作负荷普遍相关，其中时间需求和挫败感的关系最清晰。需要进一步的纵向和干预研究，以确定AI素养的提高是否伴随护士工作负荷体验的有意义变化。
